title: React Performance Guide
excerpt: Learn how to optimize React applications for better performance.
content:
React Performance Guide

React apps can slow down when components re-render unnecessarily. Understanding why re-renders happen is the first step toward building fast, responsive interfaces.

1. Memoize Expensive Calculations

Use useMemo to cache the result of expensive computations so they only re-run when their dependencies change.

When to reach for it

Only apply this when a profiler actually shows a bottleneck, since premature memoization adds complexity without benefit.

2. Stabilize Callback References

Wrap event handlers passed to child components with useCallback to prevent unnecessary child re-renders.

Common pitfall

Forgetting to include all dependencies in the array can cause stale closures, which are harder to debug than the re-renders you were trying to avoid.

3. Split Components Wisely

Break large components into smaller ones so React can skip re-rendering parts of the tree that have not changed. Combine this with React.memo for pure presentational components.

4. Virtualize Long Lists

For lists with hundreds or thousands of items, use a windowing library so only the visible rows are mounted to the DOM.

5. Code-Split with Lazy Loading

Use React.lazy and dynamic imports to split your bundle, so users only download what the current page needs.

Conclusion

Performance work is about measuring first, then applying the right technique where it actually matters.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Improve React application performance with practical techniques.

title: Understanding Redux Toolkit
excerpt: Redux Toolkit simplifies Redux development significantly.
content:
Understanding Redux Toolkit

Redux Toolkit (RTK) is the official, opinionated way to write Redux logic, removing much of the boilerplate that made plain Redux tedious.

createSlice

Instead of writing separate action types, action creators, and reducers by hand, createSlice lets you define state and reducer logic together.

Under the hood

It uses Immer internally, so you can write code that looks like it mutates state directly while staying fully immutable.

configureStore

RTK's configureStore sets up the Redux DevTools extension and useful middleware like redux-thunk automatically.

RTK Query

For data fetching, RTK Query provides hooks that handle caching, loading states, and re-fetching, removing the need for separate libraries in many projects.

Why it matters

By reducing boilerplate and enforcing best practices, Redux Toolkit makes state management more approachable for teams of any size.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Learn Redux Toolkit basics.

title: Beginner Guide to TypeScript
excerpt: Why TypeScript makes JavaScript development safer.
content:
Beginner Guide to TypeScript

TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds static typing, compiling down to plain JavaScript so it runs anywhere JavaScript does.

Why Use TypeScript?

Static types catch a whole class of bugs, like passing the wrong type to a function, before your code ever runs.

Editor benefits

Your editor can also provide much richer autocomplete and inline documentation once types are in place.

Basic Types

TypeScript supports primitives like string, number, and boolean, plus advanced constructs like interfaces, unions, and generics.

Interfaces

Interfaces let you define the shape of an object, making it clear what properties a function expects and returns.

Getting Started

You can add TypeScript to an existing project incrementally, renaming files from .js to .ts one at a time.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Learn TypeScript fundamentals.

title: Node.js Architecture Tips
excerpt: Best practices when designing scalable Node.js systems.
content:
Node.js Architecture Tips

As a Node.js application grows, a clear architecture becomes essential for keeping the codebase maintainable and testable.

Layered Structure

Separate your code into layers: controllers handle HTTP requests, services contain business logic, and repositories handle data access.

Why layers help

This separation makes each piece easier to test in isolation and easier to reason about individually.

Dependency Injection

Avoid tightly coupling modules together. Passing dependencies explicitly makes it easier to swap implementations and write unit tests with mocks.

Centralized Error Handling

Use a single error-handling middleware to catch and format errors consistently, instead of scattering try/catch blocks everywhere.

Configuration

Keep configuration in environment variables and validate them at startup so misconfiguration fails fast.

Horizontal Scalability

Design services to be stateless wherever possible so you can run multiple instances behind a load balancer.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Best architecture practices.

title: Deploy Node Apps with Docker
excerpt: Containerize your Node.js applications easily.
content:
Deploy Node Apps with Docker

Docker lets you package a Node.js application together with its dependencies and runtime, so it behaves the same everywhere.

Writing a Dockerfile

A basic Dockerfile starts from an official node base image, copies your package.json, installs dependencies, and defines the start command.

Multi-stage builds

Compile or install dev dependencies in one stage, then copy only the production artifacts into a slim final image, keeping the deployed image small and secure.

docker-compose for Local Development

A docker-compose.yml file makes it easy to spin up your app alongside supporting services like a database, with a single command.

Best Practices

Use a .dockerignore file to exclude node_modules, run your app as a non-root user, and pin base image versions for reproducible builds.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Learn Docker deployment.

title: Building REST API with Express
excerpt: Create scalable REST APIs using Express.js.
content:
Building REST API with Express

Express is a minimal and flexible Node.js web framework that makes it straightforward to build REST APIs.

Setting Up Routes

Define routes for each resource using HTTP verbs like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.

Route handlers

Each verb maps to a handler function that reads or modifies your data and sends back a response.

Middleware

Middleware functions let you handle cross-cutting concerns such as logging, authentication, and request validation in a reusable way.

Error Handling

Express supports dedicated error-handling middleware, letting you centralize how errors are logged and formatted into consistent responses.

Scaling the structure

As your API grows, use the Router class to split routes into separate files per resource, keeping app.js clean.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Build REST API with Express.

title: How to Start Coding Career
excerpt: Tips for starting a career in software development.
content:
How to Start Coding Career

Breaking into software development can feel overwhelming, but a focused plan makes the path much clearer.

Pick a Starting Language

Choose one beginner-friendly language, such as JavaScript or Python, and commit to it long enough to build real projects.

Avoid tutorial-hopping

Jumping between languages too soon is one of the most common reasons beginners never gain real depth.

Build a Portfolio

Employers care more about what you can build than certificates alone. Create a handful of small, complete projects and publish the code.

Learn the Fundamentals

Beyond syntax, understand core concepts like data structures, version control with Git, and how the web works.

Network and Apply Early

Join developer communities and start applying to junior roles before you feel fully ready, since most learning happens on the job.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Guide to start coding career.

title: Best Programming Habits
excerpt: Habits that make developers productive.
content:
Best Programming Habits

Great developers are not necessarily the ones who know the most syntax. They are the ones with consistent habits that compound over time.

Write Readable Code

Use clear naming, small functions, and consistent formatting. Code is read far more often than it is written.

Commit Often, Commit Small

Break your work into small, logical commits with descriptive messages.

Why it helps

Small commits make it much easier to review changes and roll back if something goes wrong.

Test as You Go

Writing tests alongside your code, rather than after, catches bugs early and gives you the confidence to refactor without fear.

Keep Learning

Set aside regular time to read documentation and revisit fundamentals, since the field moves quickly.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Best habits for programmers.

title: Protein Diet for Muscle Gain
excerpt: A structured protein diet for gaining lean muscle.
content:
Protein Diet for Muscle Gain

Building lean muscle requires more than just lifting weights. Your diet, especially protein intake, plays a central role in recovery and growth.

How Much Protein Do You Need?

Most people aiming to build muscle should target roughly 1.6 to 2.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day.

Spreading it out

Splitting that total across multiple meals appears to support muscle protein synthesis better than one large dose.

Best Protein Sources

Lean meats, eggs, fish, dairy, legumes, and tofu all provide high-quality protein.

Timing Matters

Including a meal shortly after training may offer a modest edge, though total daily intake matters more than exact timing.

Do Not Forget the Rest

Protein alone is not enough. Adequate calories, sleep, and progressive training are equally important.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Protein diet guide.

title: Healthy Diet Basics
excerpt: Understand the basics of a healthy diet.
content:
Healthy Diet Basics

A healthy diet does not have to be complicated. A few consistent habits can make a bigger difference than any short-term trend.

Balance Your Macronutrients

Aim for a mix of carbohydrates, protein, and healthy fats at most meals, favoring whole foods.

Watch Portion Sizes

Even healthy foods can lead to weight gain in large enough quantities.

A simpler approach

Paying attention to portions is often more sustainable than eliminating entire food groups.

Stay Hydrated

Water supports nearly every bodily function. Many people mistake mild dehydration for hunger.

Consistency Over Perfection

A sustainable diet is one you can maintain long-term. Small, consistent improvements beat short bursts of extreme restriction.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Guide to healthy diet.

title: Chocolate Cookie Recipe
excerpt: Easy homemade chocolate cookies recipe.
content:
Chocolate Cookie Recipe

These rich, chewy chocolate cookies come together in under 30 minutes with basic pantry ingredients.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 3/4 cup cocoa powder
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup brown sugar
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 cup chocolate chips

Instructions

Prep

Preheat the oven to 175C (350F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Mixing

Cream the butter and sugars together until light and fluffy, then beat in the eggs and vanilla. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt, then gradually combine the two and fold in the chocolate chips.

Baking

Scoop tablespoon-sized balls of dough onto the sheet and bake for 9 to 11 minutes, then cool on the sheet briefly before transferring to a wire rack.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Homemade cookies.

title: Strawberry Cookie Recipe
excerpt: Delicious strawberry cookies recipe.
content:
Strawberry Cookie Recipe

Soft, pink-tinted cookies with a real strawberry flavor, perfect for a sweet afternoon treat.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
  • 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/3 cup freeze-dried strawberries, crushed into powder
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp salt

Instructions

Prep

Preheat the oven to 175C (350F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Mixing

Cream the butter and sugar until fluffy, then mix in the egg and vanilla extract. Whisk the flour, crushed freeze-dried strawberries, baking powder, and salt separately, then combine without overmixing.

Baking

Roll the dough into small balls, place on the sheet, and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are just set.
author: Vincent Guizot
seoDescription: Strawberry cookie recipe.
